Question B-007-008-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Meteor scatter is most effective at the lower end of very high frequency (VHF), where ionized meteor trails redirect signals well enough for brief extended-range contacts. Below about 30 MHz, ordinary ionospheric propagation, absorption, and noise tend to dominate. The 30 MHz to 100 MHz range covers the useful meteor-scatter region.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "10 MHz to 30 MHz": That range is mid-to-upper high-frequency (HF), where ordinary ionospheric modes, absorption, and noise are more important than meteor-trail reflections.
- sourceIndex 2: "3 MHz to 10 MHz": Lower HF is much too low for the standard extended-range meteor-scatter window.
- sourceIndex 3: "100 MHz to 150 MHz": Above 100 MHz, meteor trails are less effective and openings become shorter and more demanding, so this is above the best range.
